interfaces.name: Side-push stem (Φ2, axis 1.7 mm above the board)

params.actuation: side push, parallel to the mounting face, tactile (sharp feeling type)
params.life_test: 5 V DC 5 mA resistive, 2.1 N, 2-3 operations per s

params.note: Press the centre of the stem with a flat keying tip; a Φ2 mm cylinder is recommended, tilted 3° or less. Never load the stem from the side. Loads above the specified stress break the switch (D6; stop strength 30 N for 15 s, §7.4). Only the Japanese text of D6 adds that a stopper supporting the switch is recommended if loads above the rating, or constant high loads, can reach it (our translation). The switch is for human operation, not mechanical detection. Debounce in firmware (10 ms max bounce new, 20 ms after life).
params.source: https://tech.alpsalpine.com/cms.media/product_spec_skrtlae010_en_1db35b7ed3.pdf (B3, D3, D4, D5, D6 incl. its Japanese text, D8, D9, §6.4, §7.4)

interfaces.name: Board mount (2 soldered fixing legs, 2 guide bosses)

params.note: Two frame fixing legs (0.8 ± 0.1 mm wide) at the front corners, soldered to their own lands; two guide bosses (0.7 ± 0.05 mm wide, 0.45 mm long below the mounting face, 4.25 mm apart, 2.05 ± 0.1 mm behind the stem tip) located in 2 × Φ0.9 mm board holes. The land drawing marks the area between the leg lands as prohibited for copper tracks.

Reflow only: 260 °C max for 3 s at the product surface, 150-180 °C preheat 120 s max, 40 s max above 230 °C, 2 reflows max, cream solder 0.1-0.15 mm. No flux on the terminals or board before soldering, and no washing. If the switch sits at the board edge, do not auto-dip after mounting (B4). Back-side dip soldering is otherwise allowed after reflow, but with no through holes under or around the switch (D2, §10.3(4)). Not sealed: keep dust, siloxane-emitting silicone and condensation away from it.

name: Alps Alpine SKRTLAE010 side-push TACT switch

params.note: Maximum rating 12 V DC 50 mA, resistive DC load.

params.voltage_proof: 250 V AC for 1 min between all terminals and between the terminals and the frame

params.note: Circuit: 1 pole 1 throw, normally open. Terminals 1 and 3 are joined internally; pressing the stem closes them to terminal 2.

params.reason: Design intent, not from any source: a common way to read a normally-open switch. No source assigns these pins for the watch (SW1, SW2) or the bottle (SW1); the board design decides.
params.value: terminal 2 to a GPIO input with a pull-up; terminals 1 and 3 to GND

params.note: Supply status Standard (mass-produced, recommended for new designs) on the Alps page, 2026-10-02. JLCPCB C110293, 33,262 in stock on 2026-10-02 (distributor mirror).

params.reason: The drawing's bottom view numbers ①②③ left to right but does not say which way it is viewed; read as a third-angle bottom view, which keeps left and right of the front view. Terminals 1 and 3 are common, so a mirror changes nothing electrically.
params.value: terminal 1 at -X: the left terminal looking at the stem

params.field: CAD dimensions not on the drawing
params.reason: The drawing gives the outline, stem, boss and terminal widths but not these. Positions and thicknesses are measured from the vendor STEP (src_cad, evidence only). The drawing's side view does give one riser dimension: 0.5 mm, measured up from the mounting face at the rear terminal riser, and the STEP shows the terminal tabs rising at the rear, beyond the 2.56 mm body, to 2.71 mm behind the frame face. The model leaves the riser out (flat feet only). Terminal thickness and leg height are not dimensioned on the drawing.
params.value: terminal feet 0.15 mm thick, flat on the mounting face, 1.34-2.67 mm behind the frame face (terminal 2 from 1.54); bosses and legs 0.21 mm thick; legs 0.8 mm tall with their undersides on the mounting face; housing a plain 4.5 × 2.56 × 3.25 mm box 0.05 mm above the mounting face

params.resolution: Drawing value used; the generated body is 3.3 mm high.
